alt: Five angle types drawn with their sizes: acute 40°, right 90°, obtuse 130°, straight 180° and reflex 250°, showing acute below 90°, obtuse between 90° and 180°, and reflex between 180° and 360°.
caption: Figure: acute, right, obtuse, straight and reflex angles

alt: Two parallel lines PQ and RS cut by a transversal XY: angle PXY is 64°, the alternate angle XYS is also 64°, and the co-interior angle XYR is 116°, so 64° + 116° = 180°.
caption: Figure: alternate angles are equal; co-interior angles add up to 180°

alt: A compass with the eight directions and their three-figure bearings, all measured clockwise from north: north 000°, north-east 045°, east 090°, south-east 135°, south 180°, south-west 225°, west 270° and north-west 315°.
caption: Figure: three-figure bearings run clockwise from north through 360°

alt: Farai walks 5 km due east from A to C, then 8 km due north to B: AB is 9.43 km, the bearing of B from A is 032° (tan θ = 5/8), and the back bearing of A from B is 212°, measured clockwise from the north line at B.
caption: Figure: bearings are measured clockwise from the north line at the starting point

alt: A circle with centre O and chord AB: angle AOB at the centre is 130°; angle ACB at the circumference on the major arc is half of it, 65°; angle ADB on the minor arc is 115°, and 65° + 115° = 180° because ACBD is a cyclic quadrilateral.
caption: Figure: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference

alt: Left: a sector of radius 9 cm and angle 40° (one ninth of the circle) with arc length 2π ≈ 6.28 cm and area 9π ≈ 28.3 cm². Right: a segment of a circle of radius 8 cm cut off by a chord at 60°, whose area is the sector 33.51 cm² minus the triangle 27.71 cm², about 5.80 cm².
caption: Figure: a sector is a fraction θ/360 of the circle; a segment is a sector minus a triangle

alt: Left: AB is a diameter and C is on the circle, so angle ACB is 90°; with angle CAB 34°, angle ABC is 56°. Right: the tangent at T meets the radius OT at 90°; with angle TOP 58°, angle OPT is 32°.
caption: Figure: the angle in a semicircle and the tangent-radius angle are both 90°

alt: Graph of y = 2(x − 2)² − 5: the completed-square form gives the minimum point (2, −5) on the line of symmetry x = 2, and the curve crosses the x-axis at x ≈ 0.42 and x ≈ 3.58.
caption: Figure: the turning point of y = 2(x − 2)² − 5 is (2, −5)

alt: Two compound shapes: an athletics track made of a 100 m by 64 m rectangle with a semicircle of radius 32 m on each end (perimeter 100 + 100 + π × 64 ≈ 401 m), and a silo made of a cylinder (radius 3 m, height 8 m) with a cone of height 2 m on top (volume 78π ≈ 245 m³).
caption: Figure: split a compound shape into rectangles, circles, cylinders and cones

alt: A cone with radius 6 cm and vertical height 8 cm: the radius, height and slant height form a right-angled triangle, so the slant height is l = √(6² + 8²) = 10 cm.
caption: Figure: the slant height of a cone comes from a right-angled triangle

alt: Why SSA does not prove congruence: with AB = 7 cm, angle B = 35° and AC = 5 cm, an arc of radius 5 cm centred on A cuts the line from B twice, giving two different triangles with BC = 2.8 cm and BC = 8.7 cm.
caption: Figure: two different triangles fit the same two sides and a non-included angle

alt: Constructing the perpendicular bisector of AB: arcs of the same radius, more than half of AB, are drawn from A and from B above and below the line; joining the crossing points P and Q gives a line through the midpoint M at a right angle to AB.
caption: Figure: the perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB

alt: Constructing triangle ABC from three sides: draw AB = 8 cm, then an arc of radius 7 cm from A and an arc of radius 6 cm from B; where the arcs cross is vertex C, and the construction arcs are left showing.
caption: Figure: two arcs fix the third vertex of a triangle

alt: The four quadrants of the Cartesian plane numbered anticlockwise from the top right, with one point in each: (3, 2) in the first, (−3, 2) in the second, (−3, −2) in the third and (3, −2) in the fourth, showing the signs of x and y.
caption: Figure: the four quadrants, numbered anticlockwise from the top right

alt: Triangle ABC with the standard labelling: sides b = 7 cm and c = 10 cm enclose angle A = 115°, so the cosine rule gives the opposite side a = 14.4 cm (the longest side, opposite the obtuse angle); the other angles are 26.1° and 38.9°.
caption: Figure: side a lies opposite angle A; two sides and the angle between them fix the triangle

alt: Graph of the cubic y = x³ − 3x + 1 for x from −2 to 2: the curve rises from the bottom left to a maximum near (−1, 3), falls to a minimum near (1, −1), then rises again, passing through (0, 1).
caption: Figure: a cubic curve has a maximum and a minimum

alt: Graph of y = x³ − 6x + 2 for x from −3 to 3 on a grid: the curve rises from the bottom left to a maximum near x = −1.4, falls to a minimum near x = 1.4 and rises again, crossing the x-axis three times, with the largest crossing a little above x = 2.
caption: Figure: the graph of y = x³ − 6x + 2 for −3 ≤ x ≤ 3

alt: Cumulative frequency curve for the waiting times of 80 patients through (30, 0), (40, 4), (50, 16), (60, 32), (70, 48), (80, 68) and (90, 80); dashed reading lines from 20, 40 and 60 on the vertical axis meet the curve at the lower quartile 52.7, the median 65.2 and the upper quartile 75.8 minutes.
caption: Figure: read across from n/4, n/2 and 3n/4, then down to the time axis

alt: A cylindrical tank of radius 1.2 m and height 2 m next to its curved surface unrolled into a rectangle 7.54 m long (the circumference 2π × 1.2) and 2 m high, with area 2πrh = 15.1 m².
caption: Figure: the curved surface of a cylinder unrolls into a rectangle

alt: Two graphs of simultaneous equations: 2x + 3y = 12 and x + 2y = 7 have determinant 1 and cross at the single point (3, 2); x + 2y = 7 and 2x + 4y = 6 have determinant 0 (a singular matrix) and are parallel lines with no solution.
caption: Figure: a non-zero determinant gives one crossing point, a zero determinant gives parallel lines

alt: Graph of the pen area A = 40x − 2x² against the width x: the curve peaks at x = 10 m where A = 200 m², where dA/dx = 40 − 4x = 0, so the largest pen is 10 m wide and 20 m long.
caption: Figure: the area is greatest where the gradient is zero

alt: Graph of y = x³ − 3x² − 9x + 5: the curve rises to a maximum at (−1, 10) and falls to a minimum at (3, −22); the tangents there are horizontal, so dy/dx = 3x² − 6x − 9 = 0 at x = −1 and x = 3.
caption: Figure: stationary points are where the tangent is horizontal (gradient 0)

alt: A viewing platform 110 m above a river: the angle of depression of the raft from the platform is 38°, equal to the angle of elevation of the platform from the raft (alternate angles), so the raft is 110 ÷ tan 38° = 141 m from the foot of the cliff.
caption: Figure: angle of depression at the top equals angle of elevation at the bottom

alt: Triangle ABC with A(0, 1), B(1, 1), C(0, 2) is enlarged with scale factor 3 about the centre (−1, 0) to give A′(2, 3), B′(5, 3), C′(2, 6); the rays from the centre through each vertex pass through the matching image vertex.
caption: Figure: rays from the centre through each vertex find the enlarged image

alt: A line crossing the y-axis at (0, −2) and passing through (4, 6): c is −2, the run is 4 and the rise is 8, so the gradient m is 2 and the equation is y = 2x − 2.
caption: Figure: read c at the y-axis, then find m from rise over run

alt: The two special triangles for exact trigonometric values: a right-angled isosceles triangle with legs 1 and hypotenuse √2 (angles 45°), and half an equilateral triangle with sides 1, √3 and 2 (angles 30° and 60°).
caption: Figure: the 45° triangle and the 30°–60° triangle give the exact values

alt: Difference of two squares as area: a square of side 32.5 m with a 7.5 m square removed has area 32.5² − 7.5²; cutting off the top piece and moving it to the side makes a rectangle 40 m by 25 m, so 32.5² − 7.5² = (32.5 − 7.5)(32.5 + 7.5) = 25 × 40 = 1000 m².
caption: Figure: a² − b² cut and rearranged into the rectangle (a − b)(a + b)

alt: Four sketches of lines: a line rising left to right has a positive gradient, one falling has a negative gradient, a horizontal line has gradient zero, and a vertical line has an undefined gradient.
caption: Figure: the four kinds of gradient

alt: A line through (0, 1) and (2, 7) with a right-angled triangle drawn under it: the run is 2 units across and the rise is 6 units up, so the gradient is 6 divided by 2, which is 3.
caption: Figure: gradient is rise over run, here 6 ÷ 2 = 3

alt: Histogram of the ages of 100 patients with bars of unequal width: heights are frequency densities 1.6 (0 to 10 years), 1.2 (10 to 20), 1.4 (20 to 40), 1.2 (40 to 60) and 1.0 (60 to 80); the 20 to 40 bar holds the most patients (28) but is not the tallest.
caption: Figure: the area of each bar, not its height, is the frequency

alt: Graph of y = 2ˣ: it passes through (0, 1), showing that any base to the power 0 is 1, and through (−1, 1/2) and (−2, 1/4), showing that a negative index gives a reciprocal; the curve is always above the x-axis and never negative.
caption: Figure: y = 2ˣ shows that x⁰ = 1 and that a negative index gives a small positive reciprocal

alt: Four number lines: x > 3 has an open circle at 3 and an arrow right; x ≤ −2 has a closed circle at −2 and an arrow left; −2 ≤ x < 5 is closed at −2 and open at 5; −3 < x ≤ 4 is open at −3 and closed at 4, with the integers −2 to 4 marked.
caption: Figure: open circles exclude the end value, closed circles include it

alt: Region for x ≥ 0, y ≥ 1 and x + y ≤ 5: the unwanted areas are shaded grey and the unshaded triangle R has vertices (0, 1), (0, 5) and (4, 1).
caption: Figure: shade the unwanted regions; the unshaded triangle R is the answer

alt: Distance-time curve d = 0.5t² for 0 to 10 s: the tangent at t = 6 s (through (3, 0) and (10, 42)) has gradient 6 m/s, steeper than the dashed chord from (0, 0) to (10, 50), whose gradient is the average speed of 5 m/s.
caption: Figure: the tangent gives speed at one instant, the chord gives average speed

alt: The borehole at (2, 3) and the school at (10, 9) are joined by a pipe that is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle with sides 8 and 6, so its length is √(8² + 6²) = 10 km and its midpoint is (6, 6).
caption: Figure: the length of a segment is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle

alt: Graph of 2x + 3y = 12: the line crosses the y-axis at (0, 4) and the x-axis at (6, 0), and the check point (3, 2) also lies on it.
caption: Figure: the intercepts and a check point fix the line 2x + 3y = 12

alt: Linear programming for Mr Moyo: the shaded feasible region is the quadrilateral with vertices (0, 2), (7, 2), (6, 4) and (0, 10), bounded by y = 2, 2x + y = 16, x + y = 10 and the y-axis, with a dashed search line 500x + 300y = 1500; profit is 600, 4100, 4200 and 3000, so the maximum US$4200 is at (6, 4).
caption: Figure: the feasible region and the profit at each vertex

alt: Graph of y = 2x − 3 for x from −2 to 3: the six table points (−2, −7), (−1, −5), (0, −3), (1, −1), (2, 1) and (3, 3) lie on one straight line that rises 2 units for every 1 unit across.
caption: Figure: the six points of the table lie on one ruled line

alt: The four standard loci: a circle for a fixed distance from a point; two parallel lines joined by semicircles for a fixed distance from a line segment; the perpendicular bisector for points equidistant from two points A and B; and the angle bisector for points equidistant from two lines meeting at O.
caption: Figure: the four standard loci

alt: Rectangular garden ABCD with AB = 8 m and BC = 6 m: the dashed perpendicular bisector of AB meets the quarter-circle of radius 5 m centred on A at the tap T, which is 4 m from AD and 3 m from AB, the centre of the garden.
caption: Figure: two loci cross at the tap T

alt: Two unit squares and their images: a quarter turn anticlockwise sends I(1, 0) to (0, 1) and J(0, 1) to (−1, 0), giving the matrix with columns (0, 1) and (−1, 0); a shear with the x-axis invariant and factor 3 keeps I fixed and sends J to (3, 1), giving the columns (1, 0) and (3, 1).
caption: Figure: the columns of a matrix are the images of I and J

alt: Matrix multiplication: in the product of A = (2, −1; 1, 3) and B = (3, 1; 4, −2), row 1 of A (shaded amber) times column 2 of B (shaded blue) gives the top-right element of AB, 2 × 1 + (−1) × (−2) = 4; the whole product is (2, 4; 15, −5).
caption: Figure: each element of a product is a row of the first matrix times a column of the second

alt: The four area formulas with the lesson's values: rectangle 12.5 m by 8 m has area 100 m²; triangle with base 9 cm and perpendicular height 6 cm has area 27 cm²; parallelogram with base 14 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm has area 70 cm²; trapezium with parallel sides 7 m and 11 m, 4 m apart, has area 36 m². Marked heights are perpendicular to the base, not the sloping sides.
caption: Figure: use the perpendicular height, not the sloping side

alt: The parabola y = x² + x − 5 and the straight line y = 2x + 1 cross at exactly two points, (3, 7) and (−2, −3), which are the two solutions of the simultaneous equations found from x² − x − 6 = 0.
caption: Figure: the solutions are where the line meets the curve

alt: Three small graphs of a parabola with a line: a line crossing it gives two solutions (two real roots), a line touching it gives one solution (a repeated root, y = 4x − 4 touching y = x² at (2, 4)), and a line below it gives none.
caption: Figure: two, one or no solutions depending on how the line meets the curve

alt: Unit circle (upper half): the horizontal line at height 0.6 meets the circle at two points, at 36.9° and at 180° − 36.9° = 143.1°, so sin x = 0.6 has two solutions between 0° and 180°.
caption: Figure: a positive sine value gives an acute angle and its supplement

alt: Parallelogram ABCD with A(0, 1), B(4, 3), C(5, 6) and D(1, 4): AB and DC both have gradient 0.5, and AD and BC both have gradient 3, so each pair of opposite sides is parallel.
caption: Figure: parallel sides have equal gradients

alt: Graph of the hall cost C = 90 + 5n for partial variation: a straight line with gradient 5 (US$5 per guest) that cuts the vertical axis at US$90, the fixed fee, so it does not pass through the origin; it passes through (40, 290), (70, 440) and (100, 590).
caption: Figure: partial variation is a straight line that does not start at the origin

alt: The perpendicular bisector of A(1, 2) and B(7, 6): it passes through the midpoint M(4, 4) at a right angle to AB (gradient 2/3), has gradient −3/2 and equation 3x + 2y = 20, and passes through (0, 10).
caption: Figure: the perpendicular bisector 3x + 2y = 20 meets AB at its midpoint

alt: Pie chart of the main income crop of 60 farmers: maize 27 farmers (162°), tobacco 15 (90°), cotton 10 (60°) and groundnuts 8 (48°); each farmer is 6° and the angles add up to 360°.
caption: Figure: sector angle = frequency ÷ total × 360°

alt: Left: a hexagon split from one vertex into 4 triangles, so its interior angles add up to 4 × 180° = 720°, and each angle of a regular hexagon is 120°. Right: a regular hexagon with each side extended, giving six exterior angles of 60° that add up to 360°.
caption: Figure: interior angle sum from triangles, and exterior angles that total 360°

alt: Two conversion graphs: dollars to rand at R18 per dollar is a straight line through the origin (R450 reads as US$25, gradient 18); Celsius to Fahrenheit is a straight line from (0, 32) to (100, 212) with gradient 1.8, F = 1.8C + 32, so 25°C is 77°F.
caption: Figure: the gradient of a conversion graph is the rate; the second line does not pass through the origin

alt: Three containers filled at a constant rate, with the depth-time graph beneath each: a cylinder gives a straight line, a container that widens towards the top gives a curve that gets less steep, and one that narrows towards the top gives a curve that gets steeper.
caption: Figure: the shape of the container decides the shape of the depth-time graph

alt: The probability scale from 0 (impossible) through 1/2 (even chance) to 1 (certain), with events marked: a dice showing 7 is 0, a 6 is 1/6, heads is 1/2, a number greater than 1 is 5/6 and a number less than 7 is 1.
caption: Figure: events placed on the probability scale

alt: A 6.5 m ladder leans against a vertical wall with its foot 2.5 m from the wall on level ground: the right-angled triangle gives h² = 6.5² − 2.5² = 36, so the ladder reaches 6 m up the wall.
caption: Figure: the ladder is the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle

alt: A right-angled triangle with sides 3, 4 and 5 and a square drawn on each side: the squares have areas 9, 16 and 25, and 9 + 16 = 25, which is Pythagoras' theorem.
caption: Figure: the squares on the two shorter sides add up to the square on the hypotenuse

alt: Graph of y = x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3): the curve crosses the x-axis at x = 2 and x = 3, which are the solutions of x² − 5x + 6 = 0, and meets the y-axis at (0, 6).
caption: Figure: the solutions of x² − 5x + 6 = 0 are where the curve crosses the x-axis

alt: Graph of y = x² − 2x − 3: a U-shaped curve with minimum (1, −4) that crosses the x-axis at x = −1 and x = 3; the dashed line y = 2 meets it at about x = −1.4 and x = 3.4, the solutions of x² − 2x − 3 = 2.
caption: Figure: roots and the solutions of x² − 2x − 3 = 2 read from the curve

alt: Bar model for sharing US$360 in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4: the total is 9 equal parts of US$40, so Tendai gets 2 parts = US$80, Rudo 3 parts = US$120 and Farai 4 parts = US$160, which add to US$360.
caption: Figure: a bar model shows the 9 equal parts behind the ratio 2 : 3 : 4

alt: Graph of y = 6/x: two separate smooth branches, one in the first quadrant through (1, 6), (2, 3), (3, 2) and (6, 1) and one in the third quadrant through (−2, −3); neither branch touches the axes.
caption: Figure: the reciprocal graph has two branches that never touch the axes

alt: Triangle ABC with vertices (2, 1), (5, 1) and (5, 3) reflected in the line y = x to give (1, 2), (1, 5) and (3, 5), and in the line x = −1 to give (−4, 1), (−7, 1) and (−7, 3); each image is the same distance behind the mirror line as the object is in front.
caption: Figure: reflecting a triangle in y = x and in x = −1

alt: Triangle S with vertices (1, 2), (3, 2) and (3, 3) is mapped onto triangle T with vertices (−2, 1), (−2, 3) and (−3, 3) by a rotation of 90° anticlockwise about the origin; the dashed lines from the origin to (1, 2) and (−2, 1) meet at 90°.
caption: Figure: S maps onto T by a quarter turn anticlockwise about the origin

alt: A classroom 12 m by 8 m drawn at scale 1 : 200, so 1 cm represents 2 m: the plan is a rectangle 6 cm by 4 cm and its diagonal measures about 7.2 cm, which is about 14.4 m in the real room.
caption: Figure: every length on the plan is divided by 200; angles do not change

alt: Scatter diagram of test mark against hours of revision for eight learners, from (1, 35) to (8, 72): the points rise steadily, showing strong positive correlation; the line of best fit passes through the mean point (4.5, 54) with a gradient of about 5.25 marks per hour.
caption: Figure: strong positive correlation, with the line of best fit through the mean point

alt: Difference table for the sequence 4, 11, 22, 37, 56: the first differences are 7, 11, 15, 19 and the second differences are all 4, so the nth term is quadratic with 2n² as its leading part (2n² + n + 1).
caption: Figure: a constant second difference means a quadratic nth term

alt: Triangle ABC with DE parallel to BC: AD = 4, DB = 6, AE = 3, EC = 4.5, DE = 5 and BC = 12.5 cm; the small triangle ADE is similar to ABC with scale factor 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5.
caption: Figure: a line parallel to one side makes a smaller similar triangle

alt: Graphs of y = 2x − 3 and y = −x + 9: the two straight lines cross at (4, 5), so x = 4 and y = 5 is the solution of the simultaneous equations.
caption: Figure: the solution is where the two lines meet

alt: Sketch of y = (x + 2)(x − 1)(x − 3): a cubic that starts at the bottom left, crosses the x-axis at x = −2, rises to a maximum, passes through (0, 6), crosses at x = 1, dips to a minimum, then crosses at x = 3 and rises.
caption: Figure: a cubic with three roots, crossing the axis at each

alt: Sketch of y = x² − 6x + 8: a U-shaped curve through (0, 8), crossing the x-axis at (2, 0) and (4, 0), with its minimum at (3, −1) on the dashed line of symmetry x = 3.
caption: Figure: sketch with the intercepts, line of symmetry and turning point labelled

alt: Two prisms: a cuboid 8 cm by 5 cm by 3 cm with volume 8 × 5 × 3 = 120 cm³ and surface area 158 cm², and a ridge tent that is a triangular prism 3 m long whose triangular cross-section (base 2.4 m, height 1.6 m) has area 1.92 m², giving a volume of 5.76 m³.
caption: Figure: volume of a prism = area of cross-section × length

alt: Left: the unit-sized square with corners (1, 1) to (2, 2) is stretched with factor 3 and the y-axis invariant, giving the rectangle from (3, 1) to (6, 2) whose area is 3 times larger. Right: rectangle OABC with B(3, 2) is sheared with factor 2 and the x-axis invariant, giving a parallelogram with B′(7, 2) and C′(4, 2) and the same area, 6.
caption: Figure: a stretch changes area by its factor; a shear keeps the area

alt: Graph of y = x² with the tangent at P(2, 4) drawn as a straight line touching the curve only at P and passing through (1, 0) and (3, 8); its gradient is 8 divided by 2, which is 4.
caption: Figure: the gradient of the tangent at P estimates the gradient of the curve

alt: A cuboid with AB = 8 cm, BC = 6 cm and AE = 5 cm: the base diagonal AC = 10 cm and the space diagonal AG = √125 = 11.2 cm are the sides of the right-angled triangle ACG (right angle at C), and the angle between AG and the base is 26.6°.
caption: Figure: the right-angled triangle ACG inside the cuboid

alt: Distance-time graph of Tatenda's cycle ride: 9 km out in 30 minutes (18 km/h), stationary for 15 minutes (the horizontal section), then 9 km back home in 30 minutes, reaching home at 75 minutes.
caption: Figure: gradient is speed; the flat section is time at rest

alt: Speed-time graph of a car: it accelerates from rest to 20 m/s in 10 s, holds 20 m/s until 40 s, then slows to rest at 48 s; the areas under the graph are 100 m, 600 m and 80 m, giving a total distance of 780 m.
caption: Figure: the area under a speed-time graph is the distance travelled

alt: Tree diagram for two counters taken without replacement from 3 red and 7 blue: first branches red 3/10 and blue 7/10; after red the second branches are red 2/9 and blue 7/9, after blue they are red 3/9 and blue 6/9; the four path probabilities are 6/90, 21/90, 21/90 and 42/90, which add up to 1.
caption: Figure: multiply along the branches; add the paths that give the result you want

alt: Cross-section of a roof: each side slopes at 28° and the ridge is 3.2 m above the walls; the right-angled triangle gives the horizontal distance x = 3.2 ÷ tan 28° = 6.02 m and the sloping side s = 3.2 ÷ sin 28° = 6.82 m.
caption: Figure: the roof splits into right-angled triangles for tan and sin

alt: Graphs of y = sin x and y = cos x from 0° to 360°: sine starts at 0, peaks at 1 at 90°, crosses 0 at 180°, bottoms at −1 at 270°; cosine starts at 1, crosses 0 at 90°, reaches −1 at 180° and returns to 1 at 360°; both have period 360°.
caption: Figure: sine and cosine are the same wave shifted by 90°

alt: A right-angled triangle with a 35° angle: the hypotenuse H is 12 cm, A is the side next to the 35° angle, O is the side opposite it, and x = O = 12 sin 35° = 6.88 cm; the ratios are sin = O/H, cos = A/H, tan = O/A.
caption: Figure: name the sides from the angle you are using, then pick sin, cos or tan

alt: Graph of y = sin x with the horizontal line y = 0.4: the line crosses the first hump at x = 23.6° and x = 156.4° (that is 180° − 23.6°), the two solutions of sin x = 0.4 between 0° and 360°.
caption: Figure: the line y = 0.4 meets the sine curve twice, symmetrically about 90°

alt: Graph of y = tan x from 0° to 360°: three rising branches through (0, 0), (180, 0) and (360, 0), with vertical asymptotes (dashed) at x = 90° and x = 270° where tan x is undefined; the period is 180°.
caption: Figure: tan x repeats every 180° and has asymptotes at 90° and 270°

alt: A square of side 1 m, which is also 100 cm: it splits into 10 × 10 = 100 squares of 10 cm by 10 cm (100 cm² each), so 1 m² = 100 × 100 = 10 000 cm²; area units convert with the length factor squared.
caption: Figure: 1 m² is 10 000 cm², because the length factor 100 is squared

alt: Two graphs of variation: the stone's distance d = 5t² rises ever more steeply through (1, 5), (2, 20), (3, 45) and (4, 80); the journey time t = 240 ÷ v falls as speed rises, passing through (80, 3) and (96, 2.5).
caption: Figure: direct variation with the square (left) and inverse variation (right)

alt: Triangle OAB with OA = a and OB = b: AB = b − a, the midpoint M of AB has OM = ½a + ½b, and the point P with AP : PB = 1 : 2 has OP = ⅔a + ⅓b.
caption: Figure: routes from O to the midpoint M and to the point P that divides AB in the ratio 1 : 2

alt: The ranger's walk from camp O: first (3, 4) km, a distance of 5 km to P, then (−5, 2) km, 5.39 km to Q; her total displacement is (−2, 6) km, so she is √40 = 6.32 km from camp although she walked 10.4 km.
caption: Figure: the magnitude of the total displacement is shorter than the distance walked

alt: Parallelogram PQRS with P(1, 1), Q(5, 2), R(6, 5) and S(2, 4): the opposite sides PQ and SR are equal vectors (4, 1) and PS and QR are equal vectors (1, 3), so S is found by moving (4, 1) back from R.
caption: Figure: opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal vectors

alt: Venn diagram for 40 learners: 18 play football only, 7 play both football and netball, 11 play netball only and 4 play neither; the football circle totals 25 and the netball circle totals 18.
caption: Figure: fill the overlap first, then the 'only' regions, then the outside

alt: Venn diagram of 30 learners: Geography only 13, both subjects 5, History only 9 and neither 3, so P(Geography only) = 13/30 and P(G or H) = 27/30 = 9/10.
caption: Figure: fill in the overlap first, then each region and the outside

alt: Venn diagram of the prime factors of 84 and 120: the overlap holds 2, 2 and 3, so the HCF is 12; 84 alone has 7; 120 alone has 2 and 5; multiplying all the numbers in the diagram gives the LCM 840.
caption: Figure: the overlap multiplies to the HCF; everything multiplies to the LCM

alt: Venn diagram of 50 people: tea only 20, both 8, coffee only 12 and neither 10; given that a person drinks coffee, only the circle C (20 people) counts, and 8 of them also drink tea, so the probability is 8/20 = 2/5.
caption: Figure: given coffee, only the shaded circle C (20 people) is possible
